foundation_sources.citation: Naoki Masuda, Mason A. Porter, and Renaud Lambiotte, Random walks and diffusion on networks, Physics Reports 716-717 (2017)
foundation_sources.entails: With row probability evolution, T=D^-1 A and the random-walk normalized Laplacian is D^-1 L=I-T, where L=D-A.
foundation_sources.limitation: The displayed section is a continuous-time formulation; the matrix identity and row convention are the relevant claims.

foundation_sources.citation: Daniel A. Spielman, Graphs and Networks, Lecture 4: Random Walks on Graphs (2006)
foundation_sources.entails: D^(1/2) M D^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2) A D^(-1/2), a symmetric matrix. Subtracting from I gives the corresponding similarity between L_rw and L_sym.
foundation_sources.limitation: The notes use unweighted degrees in this lecture; the same algebra holds for symmetric positive conductance matrices.
foundation_sources.locator: PDF p.1, definition M=D^-1 A and p_t=p_(t-1)M; PDF p.2, similarity derivation

foundation_sources.citation: Fan R. K. Chung, Lectures on Spectral Graph Theory
foundation_sources.entails: The symmetric normalized Laplacian and the random-walk transition representation are related by similarity, not equality on irregular graphs.
foundation_sources.limitation: Chung adopts a zero convention for inverse degree at isolates for the symmetric normalized object; version 1 deliberately leaves P and L_rw undefined if any isolate is present.
foundation_sources.locator: PDF p.5 / book p.2 for L_sym=T^(-1/2) L T^(-1/2); PDF p.18 / book p.15 for P=T^-1 A=T^(-1/2)(I-L_sym)T^(1/2)

foundation_sources.citation: David A. Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth L. Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, 2nd ed.
foundation_sources.entails: pi=pi P defines stationarity. Irreducibility and aperiodicity are the hypotheses for convergence from every state in the finite setting; a period-two chain alternates support and need not converge.
foundation_sources.limitation: The degree example is stated for unweighted simple walk; the weighted version follows from detailed balance and is stated in the same book's network chapter.
foundation_sources.locator: book p.9, equation (1.14), stationary definition; book p.10, equation (1.16), degree-proportional example; book pp.7-8, period and even-cycle oscillation; book p.52, Theorem 4.9

foundation_sources.citation: Levin and Peres with Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, 2nd ed.
foundation_sources.entails: For a connected weighted network, P(x,y)=c(x,y)/c(x), pi(x)=c(x)/c_G, and c_G=sum_x c(x)=2 sum_e c(e) when there are no loops.
foundation_sources.limitation: The chapter defines a network to be connected; disconnected componentwise use needs separate scoping.

foundation_sources.citation: Levin and Peres with Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, 2nd ed.
foundation_sources.entails: Currents depend on voltage differences; adding a constant changes no current. Grounding the sink at zero fixes the gauge, and unit source-to-sink flow makes the source-sink voltage difference the effective resistance.
foundation_sources.limitation: The sourced network is connected. Version 1's same-component extension is a conservative scoped computation.

foundation_sources.citation: Levin and Peres with Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, 2nd ed.
foundation_sources.entails: Commute is E_a tau_b + E_b tau_a and equals c_G R(a<->b), with c_G=sum_x c(x)=2 sum_e c(e).
foundation_sources.limitation: Connected-network theorem; hitting times can be asymmetric.

foundation_sources.citation: Chandra, Raghavan, Ruzzo, Smolensky, and Tiwari, The electrical resistance of a graph captures its commute and cover times
foundation_sources.entails: For transitions proportional to conductance, the generalized commute cost is F times effective resistance; unit directed-step costs make F the sum of weighted degrees.
foundation_sources.limitation: The section assumes a connected undirected graph.

foundation_sources.citation: Daniel A. Spielman, More Effective Resistance (2018)
foundation_sources.entails: For a connected weighted graph, the product of nonzero combinatorial-Laplacian eigenvalues is n times the sum over spanning trees of the products of their edge weights.
foundation_sources.limitation: Disconnected handling is obtained directly from the absence of spanning trees and Laplacian nullity, not from the connected theorem statement.

foundation_sources.citation: Daniel A. Spielman, More Effective Resistance (2018)
foundation_sources.entails: Under spanning-tree sampling proportional to the product of edge weights, an existing edge e appears with probability w_e R_eff(e).
foundation_sources.limitation: The theorem quantifies edges of a connected graph; it does not license a nonedge probability by inventing a weight.

scope: Authoritative source URLs, exact locators, snapshot hashes, and stated limitations for the structured checker conventions and the fixed 24-result retrieval review.
scope_limits: The 24 retrieval results are purposively fixed and do not estimate a service population rate.
Source-only labels assess supplied generated slogans against exact-version sources; they do not certify a general natural-language system.
Structured instance outputs cannot revise source-only labels and do not prove theorems.
The historical reviewer/adjudicator model string is withdrawn as unverified runtime metadata by the additive correction.
